newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche gets European enzyme patent.
newsitem.headline: Roche gets European enzyme patent.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said that the European Patent Office has awarded F.Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd a European patent which covers enzymes used in the polymerase chain reaction.
The polymerase chain reaction figures in a wide range of processes, including medical diagnostics of infectious agents, genetic disorders, cancer and other abnormalities.
"The patent grant is one of the final key elements in completing the large patent portfolio owned by Roche in the area of nucleic acid amplification technology," Roche said.
It said the patent covered native and recombinant thermostable enzymes with DNA polymerase activity "without limitation to a particular species or genus."
Thermostable enzymes are used to allow accurate DNA replication at changing temperatures, it said.
The polymerase chain reaction technology allows minute amounts of genetic material to be amplified into "billions of copies in just a few hours," Roche said.
Roche products using the polymerase chain reaction include its Amplicor HIV-1 Monitor, and Cobas Amplicor.
